purpose: Verbatim public-domain quotations cleared for use in deep verse studies. bin/verse-study-gate.js checks every quoted blockquote against the repo's own corpora first (LBCF, Baptist Catechism, Calvin's Institutes, the chapter store); anything outside those must appear here, verbatim, with verified:true, or the gate refuses the page.
rules: Paste the text exactly as printed in the source edition, including its punctuation and any printer's oddities. Do not tidy it.
verified:true means a human or agent actually opened the cited edition and read this sentence there. It does not mean the quote sounded right.
verified:false entries are a record of what was attempted and failed. The gate treats them as failures, on purpose.
If a quote will not verify, do not paraphrase it inside quotation marks. Describe the argument in your own prose and cite the work without quoting.

quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.text: To expound the term "beginning," of Christ, is altogether frivolous. For Moses simply intends to assert that the world was not perfected at its very commencement, in the manner in which it is now seen, but that it was created an empty chaos of heaven and earth.
quotes.note: Two contiguous sentences, confirmed adjacent in the CCEL text.

quotes.author: John Calvin
quotes.text: He moreover teaches by the word "created," that what before did not exist was now made; for he has not used the term יצר, (yatsar,) which signifies to frame or form, but ברא, (bara,) which signifies to create. … Therefore his meaning is, that the world was made out of nothing.
quotes.note: Two sentences from the same passage, joined with an ellipsis on the page. The CCEL edition prints 'which signifies to frame or forms but' — an evident typo in that edition, corrected to 'to frame or form, but' here and on the page. Wording is otherwise as printed.

quotes.author: Matthew Henry
quotes.text: The manner in which this work was effected: God created it, that is, made it out of nothing. … There was not any pre-existent matter out of which the world was produced.
quotes.note: Printed as '(3.) The manner in which this work was effected: _God created it,_ that is, made it out of nothing.' Enumerator and italics dropped; wording untouched. The second sentence sits about 80 words later in Henry's text, so the ellipsis is required — without it the page would imply a continuity the source does not have.

quotes.author: Matthew Henry
quotes.text: Before the beginning of time there was none but that Infinite Being that inhabits eternity.

quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.text: I boldly say, That before God made heaven and earth, He made not anything.
quotes.note: Could not be confirmed. Three sources tried on 2026-08-17 — ccel.org/ccel/augustine/confessions.xiv.xii.html (returned navigation only), confess.xiii.xii.html and confess.xiii.xiii.html (chapter text, phrase absent) — plus Gutenberg #3296, whose HTML stops in Book IV. Removed from genesis-1-1.html and replaced with unquoted prose. Restore only after reading it in a real edition of Book XI.

quotes.author: Augustine
quotes.text: Before the times created by God, times were not… Or what times should those be which were not made by You?
quotes.note: Same failed verification pass as the quote above. Do not restore without a real source.
